items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: the players that I love, Bird and Cannonball Adderley and Hank Mobley and I mean they’re all so steeped in the blues. And so through transcribing them

ctx.x: I’m fascinated by the blues and how so many early rock & roll songs were just sped up blues. And do you spend time with, especially your freshman students, playing the blues?

Yeah. And I mean, I mean the blues itself as a song form, the blues it’s a great vehicle. If we were here together we could say it’s a great thing, “Hey let’s play a blues.” There’s always going to be a blues in a set list or a jam session, right? So it’s a great conversation starter, you can think of that. But you know also, the players that I love, Bird and Cannonball Adderley and Hank Mobley and I mean they’re all so steeped in the blues. And so through transcribing them, either an actual blues or just in…

I’d like to talk about your composing for a bit. I’ve been listening to some of your recent works, “Search for a New Light” and I like the adjectives or your description of chord voicings and you’re using the terms dark and bright and drama.
